🗺️ Unit 10 Quiz: Buyer Personas & Journey Mapping

Test your understanding of buyer personas and journey mapping

0 correct
Question 1 of 10
What is the key difference between market segments and buyer personas?
A Segments are for marketing, personas are for sales
B Segments identify which companies to target; personas identify which people within those companies matter
C Segments are based on data, personas are based on assumptions
D There is no meaningful difference—they are interchangeable terms

Segments tell you WHICH COMPANIES to target (industry, size, geography). Personas tell you WHICH PEOPLE within those companies matter and how to reach them. You need both for effective B2B marketing.

Question 2 of 10
According to Gartner, how many decision-makers are typically involved in B2B enterprise purchases?
A 2-3 people
B 4-5 people
C 6-7 people
D 10-12 people

Gartner research shows an average of 6.8 decision-makers are involved in B2B purchases. This is why understanding buying committees and multi-threading across stakeholders is critical for enterprise sales.

Question 3 of 10
Which buying committee role has the power to "say yes when everyone else says no"?
A Technical Buyer
B Economic Buyer
C Champion
D User Buyer

The Economic Buyer controls the budget and can approve purchases even when other stakeholders have concerns. They're typically VP+ or C-level and care most about ROI, risk, and strategic alignment.

Question 4 of 10
What type of content does a CFO typically respond best to?
A Detailed technical architecture diagrams
B Feature comparison matrices
C Quantified business outcomes with proof points
D Hands-on product demos

CFOs are measured on financial outcomes, not features. "AI-powered analytics" means nothing to them. "Reduce days-to-close from 10 to 4, freeing your team for strategic analysis" means everything. Lead with metrics, back with proof points.

Question 5 of 10
At which journey stage is the Champion LEAST engaged?
A Awareness
B Consideration
C Purchase
D Decision

Champions are highly engaged across most stages—Awareness, Consideration, Decision, and Adoption. Their engagement typically dips during Purchase when procurement and legal take over the process mechanics.

Question 6 of 10
Why is "multi-threading" critical in enterprise sales?
A It allows you to send more emails to prospects
B It helps you bypass procurement processes
C Deals depending on a single champion are fragile—if that person leaves or loses influence, the deal dies
D It reduces the need for persona-specific content

Single-threaded deals are risky. When your one champion gets promoted, goes on leave, or loses influence, your deal evaporates. Multi-threading builds relationships across the buying committee so you're not "one reorg away from starting over."

Question 7 of 10
What is the primary concern of a Chief Data Officer (CDO)?
A Reducing headcount costs
B Data quality, governance, and demonstrating data ROI
C Supply chain resilience and logistics
D Employee experience and retention

CDOs focus on data quality, governance frameworks, AI readiness, breaking down data silos, and demonstrating ROI from data investments. They're often measured on how well they enable data-driven decision-making across the organization.

Question 8 of 10
Which persona type is most engaged during the Adoption phase of the buyer journey?
A C-Suite (CFO, CIO)
B Procurement
C End Users and Technical Buyers
D Economic Buyers

During Adoption, the focus shifts to implementation and value realization. End Users (who use the product daily) and Technical Buyers (who support it) are most engaged. C-Suite and Procurement typically step back once the deal is closed.

Question 9 of 10
What makes a buyer persona "effective" versus "generic"?
A Including demographic details like age and hobbies
B Using a professional stock photo
C Capturing specific tensions, trade-offs, and priorities that differentiate your buyers from broad stereotypes
D Making them as broad as possible to cover more prospects

Generic personas lead to generic content. Effective personas surface SPECIFIC tensions—like a CIO who's skeptical of "transformation" messaging because their last cloud project ran 40% over budget. That specificity drives differentiated, resonant messaging.

Question 10 of 10
How often should buyer personas be reviewed and updated?
A Once when created, then left as a permanent reference
B Annually during strategic planning
C Quarterly, based on win/loss insights, market changes, and sales feedback
D Only when launching a new product

Personas aren't a one-time project. Schedule quarterly reviews to update them based on new win/loss insights, changing market conditions, and sales feedback. A persona document from years ago is worse than useless—it gives false confidence while being dangerously outdated.
